feedback: Pre-race review of the iteration 5 candidate. It keeps the iteration 4 design (narrow five-sensor array at x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03; sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2]; kp 2.5; kd 0.3; ki 0; last_direction) and changes one variable, base_speed from 1.1 to 0.9. Iteration 4 is the best raced design at 302.3. Against iteration 1 at base_speed 1.3, the drop to 1.1 raised oval completion from 3/20 to 11/20, cut oval line_loss_events from 1.25 to 0.95, and lowered oval max_error from 0.061 to 0.054. Line loss remains on every track (s-bend 1.25, slalom 1.15), so the same direction is the next logical test. Iteration 2 showed that widening the array to 22.5 mm spacing lowered the score (81.1), so the narrow geometry stays. Iteration 3 showed that kp 2.2 with kd 0.25 scored lower (106.7), so kp 2.5 and kd 0.3 are held. The candidate is valid and within contract limits. Expected direction: oval mean finish time was 1.97 s at 1.1, so there is margin under 3.0 s, but a further speed drop will lengthen the run, so completion_time must be checked. Decision: approve. This is a clean single-variable step from the best design, and it gives the telemetry needed to separate speed effects from gain effects. Next race: if line_loss_events on the oval and s-bend fall below about 0.5 and completions hold near 50% or higher, keep base_speed near 0.9 and test kd 0.25 alone. If line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error near 0.054 to 0.06, speed is not the main limit, so return to base_speed 1.1 and test kp 2.0 with kd 0.3 as a separate change. If the runs finish with completion_time above 2.8 s, raise base_speed to about 1.0 rather than going back to 1.1.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events on the oval and s-bend fall to 0.5 or less and completions stay near 50% or higher, keep the narrow geometry, kp 2.5, ki 0, and base_speed 0.9, and test kd 0.25 by itself, since oval steering_oscillation was 0.33 at kd 0.3 in iteration 4.

If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more with max_error near 0.054 to 0.06 at base_speed 0.9, speed is not the main limit: return to base_speed 1.1 and try kp 2.0 with kd 0.3 as a separate single-variable change, since iteration 4 is the only controlled speed comparison.

If runs complete with completion_time above 2.8 s, raise base_speed to about 1.0 rather than 1.1, since the iteration 4 oval mean finish time was 1.97 s at base_speed 1.1 and the 3.0 s limit needs roughly 1.5 m/s average.
